artifacts.summary: Split four oversized eager rules into pre-action cores plus lazy companions, relocated CSLib /pr content, cut the literature merge-source's redundant subsection, redeployed and re-measured the eager prefix from 80,808 B to 70,160 B, and recorded a 24,000 B eager budget ceiling in context-layers.md.

completion_data.completion_summary: Reduced the session-start eager context prefix from 80,808 B to 70,160 B (-13.2%) via a four-rule split-and-relocate pass, a CSLib /pr content relocation, and a literature merge-source cut, then recorded a numeric eager budget ceiling. Two pre-existing, out-of-territory verify-deploy.sh failures were investigated, attributed via git log to predate this task, and reported rather than absorbed (Phase 7 closed as COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS with a full Reasoned Exclusions record).

memory_candidates.content: Eager/lazy rule-split pattern for this repo's rules/*.md files: when a rule's paths: frontmatter is absent, specs/**/*, .claude/**/*, or "**/*" (all of which load eagerly in a representative session), and the file has grown large, split it into a short eager core (kept in rules/) plus a lazily-loaded companion under context/standards/ (or an existing context/reference/ doc if one already serves as that rule's elaboration home -- check before creating a third file). KEEP eager, verbatim: every forbidden-operations list, write-gating prohibition, and terminal-state restriction -- these are pre-action-binding, an agent must know them before acting. MOVE to the companion: mechanism detail, per-scenario elaboration, lifecycle descriptions, and reactive recovery narrative -- useful only after something has already happened. Always run a grep reference sweep (grep -rn "<rulename>" agent-system/extensions/) both before and after the split, since other files may name a specific heading as "the authoritative home" of some rule; keep that heading in the eager core even if its elaboration moves. Every new companion file needs an index-entries.json entry (line_count from wc -l) or check-extension-docs.sh Rule S fails after the next deploy.

When a redeploy (deploy-headless.sh) surfaces verify-deploy.sh or check-extension-docs.sh failures that are unrelated to the current task's own edits, do not silently fix them out of territory. First confirm via git log/git show whether the offending file or field predates the task's own Phase 1 baseline commit -- if so, it is pre-existing drift, not a regression this task caused. Report it explicitly (a #### Reasoned Exclusions table with Item | Reason | Evidence columns, per plan-format.md's COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS mechanism) rather than absorbing an unrelated fix into this task's commits. .claude/ is git-ignored in this repo, so drift attribution for the deployed tree cannot use git diff directly -- instead rely on verify-deploy.sh's content-hash-equality check (proves deployed == source for everything this task touched) plus the task's own per-phase commit history in agent-system/extensions/**.

A backgrounded verify-deploy.sh or deploy-headless.sh run can produce a transient extra failure (observed: tests/run-all.sh reporting FAIL) when a second deploy-headless.sh runs concurrently with an in-flight verify-deploy.sh -- likely file-lock or mid-write contention, not a real regression. If a verify-deploy.sh run reports an unexpected NEW failure beyond the known/expected set, re-run it cleanly (no concurrent deploy in flight) before concluding it is a real defect; a clean re-run resolved the spurious failure here with 42/42 test suites passing.
